approvedIndications: Relief of mild to moderate pain (e.g. headache, toothache, muscle aches)

contraindications.explanation: Paracetamol is metabolized in the liver; overdose or impaired liver function can lead to fatal hepatic necrosis.
Risk of severe allergic reaction or skin reactions.

ageRestrictions.warning: Infants under 3 months should only receive paracetamol on direct advice of a pediatrician or physician.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Considered the preferred first-line analgesic/antipyretic during pregnancy when clinically needed, at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration. Consult your healthcare provider.

interactions.effect: Prolonged regular paracetamol use may enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk.
Combining multiple cough/cold or pain medicines containing paracetamol can lead to accidental toxic overdose.

commonSideEffects: Generally well tolerated at therapeutic doses
administrationWarnings: Never exceed the maximum recommended daily dose (typically 4000 mg for adults in 24 hours).
Do not take with other medicines containing paracetamol simultaneously.
Seek medical advice if pain lasts more than 5 days or fever lasts more than 3 days.
Avoid chronic excessive alcohol intake while taking paracetamol.
dosageDisclaimer: Individual dosages (mg or ml) must be determined by a registered pharmacist or physician based on patient age, weight, and renal status. Always check the manufacturer packaging leaflet.

referenceSource.name: Ghana Ministry of Health Standard Treatment Guidelines / Ghana FDA

approvedIndications: Prevention and treatment of dehydration caused by acute diarrhea and vomiting

contraindications.condition: Severe dehydration with shock or unconsciousness
contraindications.explanation: Severe dehydration is a medical emergency requiring immediate intravenous fluid resuscitation in a hospital.
Inability to retain fluids orally requires parenteral rehydration at a clinical facility.

ageRestrictions.warning: Safe for all ages including neonates, but infants with diarrhea must be monitored closely by a healthcare professional.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Safe and recommended for dehydration during pregnancy and lactation.

commonSideEffects: Mild nausea if consumed too rapidly
administrationWarnings: Always reconstitute the entire sachet in the exact volume of clean drinking water specified on the packet (usually 1 liter or 500 ml).
Do not boil the solution after preparation.
Discard any unused reconstituted solution after 24 hours.
Seek immediate medical attention if child exhibits signs of severe dehydration: sunken eyes, lethargy, or inability to drink.
dosageDisclaimer: Administer frequently in small sips following each loose stool as directed on the sachet. Consult a pharmacist or clinical officer for infants.

referenceSource.name: WHO Guidelines / Ghana National Diarrheal Disease Control Program

approvedIndications: Relief of inflammatory pain (e.g. arthritis, dental pain, dysmenorrhea/period pain)
Reduction of fever where paracetamol is insufficient

contraindications.condition: Active peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding
contraindications.explanation: NSAIDs inhibit gastric prostaglandin synthesis and may cause life-threatening gastrointestinal perforation or hemorrhage.
Risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus and prolonged labor.

contraindications.condition: Known NSAID or Aspirin-induced asthma / severe allergy
contraindications.explanation: Risk of acute bronchospasm and anaphylactoid shock.

contraindications.condition: Severe heart failure or severe renal failure
contraindications.explanation: Fluid retention and worsening renal ischemia.

ageRestrictions.warning: Not recommended for infants under 3 months or weighing less than 5 kg without direct pediatrician supervision.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Avoid during pregnancy, strictly contraindicated during the third trimester. Paracetamol is generally preferred. Consult your obstetrician.

interactions.effect: Substantially increases the risk of severe gastrointestinal and internal bleeding.
Concurrent use increases ulcer risk and attenuates the cardioprotective effect of low-dose aspirin.
Decreases antihypertensive efficacy and increases acute kidney injury risk.

administrationWarnings: Always take with or immediately after food to minimize stomach irritation.
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration possible.
Stop immediately and seek emergency care if you experience black tarry stools or vomit blood.
dosageDisclaimer: Dosage varies strictly by patient weight, age, and renal status. Consult a licensed pharmacist or physician for appropriate dosing.

referenceSource.name: Ghana MoH Standard Treatment Guidelines / Ghana FDA Register

approvedIndications: Symptomatic relief of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose, itchy watery eyes)
Relief of chronic urticaria (hives and skin allergy itching)

contraindications.explanation: Cetirizine is primarily excreted unchanged by the kidneys; dose accumulation may cause severe sedation.
Risk of acute hypersensitivity reactions.

ageRestrictions.warning: Children aged under 2 years require pediatric evaluation prior to antihistamine administration.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Animal studies do not indicate direct harm, but should only be used in pregnancy if clinically necessary and approved by an obstetrician.

interactions.effect: May enhance sedation, drowsiness, and impair mental alertness.

commonSideEffects: Mild drowsiness or fatigue in sensitive individuals
administrationWarnings: Although less sedating than first-generation antihistamines, patients should exercise caution when driving or operating machinery.
Avoid alcohol during treatment.
dosageDisclaimer: Follow the product packaging leaflet. Consult a pharmacist for pediatric dosing.

approvedIndications: Treatment of acute uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum

contraindications.explanation: Severe malaria (cerebral malaria, severe anemia, respiratory distress) is a life-threatening emergency requiring injectable artesunate in hospital.

contraindications.condition: First trimester of pregnancy (unless no alternative ACT exists)
contraindications.explanation: Oral quinine plus clindamycin is typically the preferred first-trimester guideline in Ghana unless clinician directs otherwise.

contraindications.condition: Pre-existing cardiac arrhythmia or QT prolongation
contraindications.explanation: Lumefantrine may prolong the QTc interval.

ageRestrictions.warning: Infants weighing under 5 kg must be evaluated and managed by a qualified pediatrician.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: In Ghana, ACTs are approved for uncomplicated malaria in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters. In the 1st trimester, consult a clinician for guideline-directed therapy.

interactions.effect: Substantially increases lumefantrine serum levels and risk of cardiac dysrhythmias.

commonSideEffects: Loss of appetite, mild abdominal discomfort
administrationWarnings: MUST BE PRECEDED BY A LABORATORY TEST: In Ghana, antimalarial policy strictly requires confirming malaria parasites (via RDT or microscopy) before treatment.
Take with meals or drinks containing fat (e.g. milk, soup) to ensure adequate lumefantrine absorption.
The full 3-day course of 6 doses must be completed even if symptoms resolve quickly.
Clinix does not prescribe or dispense antimalarials. Please see a healthcare professional.
dosageDisclaimer: Dosing depends on precise patient weight band (5-14kg, 15-24kg, 25-34kg, >35kg) over a strict 6-dose schedule. A pharmacist or clinic must calculate and supervise this.

referenceSource.name: Ghana National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) / MoH Guidelines

approvedIndications: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections (e.g. otitis media, streptococcal pharyngitis, community-acquired pneumonia, urinary tract infections)

contraindications.condition: Severe hypersensitivity / anaphylaxis to penicillins or beta-lactams
contraindications.explanation: Risk of life-threatening anaphylactic shock, laryngeal edema, or severe cutaneous reactions.
High incidence of generalized maculopapular rash when given during EBV infection.

ageRestrictions.warning: Pediatric formulation and weight-based dosing must be verified by a medical doctor or clinical pharmacist.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Generally considered acceptable during pregnancy when clinically indicated. Must be prescribed by a physician.

interactions.effect: Amoxicillin reduces methotrexate renal clearance, increasing methotrexate toxicity risk.

administrationWarnings: PRESCRIPTION ONLY: Antibiotics must never be taken without a formal clinical examination and valid prescription.
Amoxicillin is completely ineffective against viral infections such as colds, flu, or simple viral coughs.
Complete the entire prescribed duration to prevent antimicrobial resistance.
Clinix does not prescribe or calculate doses for antibiotics.
dosageDisclaimer: Dosage must be determined solely by an authorized medical practitioner. Clinix does not calculate antibiotic dosages.

referenceSource.name: Ghana MoH Standard Treatment Guidelines / WHO Essential Medicines

approvedIndications: Symptomatic relief of acid indigestion, heartburn, and dyspepsia

contraindications.explanation: Risk of hypermagnesemia and aluminum accumulation.
Antacids mask acute surgical abdomen signs.

ageRestrictions.warning: Not recommended for children under 6 years without medical consultation.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Generally considered acceptable for short-term heartburn in pregnancy, but avoid high chronic doses. Consult a midwife or doctor.

interactions.effect: Antacids bind antibiotics in the stomach, severely preventing their absorption. Space apart by at least 2 hours.
Decreased iron absorption. Space by at least 2 hours.

administrationWarnings: Chew tablets thoroughly before swallowing or mix powder with water as directed.
Do not take within 2 hours of taking other oral medications.
If heartburn or indigestion persists for more than 14 days, see a doctor to rule out ulcer disease or cardiac causes.
dosageDisclaimer: Follow packaging instructions. Consult your pharmacist if symptoms recur frequently.

approvedIndications: Adult relief of mild to moderate pain and headache
Cardiovascular secondary prevention (low-dose under medical supervision only)

contraindications.condition: Children and teenagers under 16 years of age
contraindications.explanation: Strictly contraindicated due to the risk of Reye's syndrome—a rare but potentially fatal condition causing acute encephalopathy and liver fatty degeneration.

contraindications.condition: Active peptic ulceration or bleeding disorders
contraindications.explanation: Irreversible platelet inhibition significantly worsens hemorrhage.
Risk of maternal and fetal bleeding and delayed labor.

ageRestrictions.warning: DO NOT GIVE TO CHILDREN OR ADOLESCENTS UNDER 16 YEARS due to the established risk of Reye's syndrome.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: High-dose analgesic aspirin is contraindicated in pregnancy, especially during the 3rd trimester. Low-dose preventive aspirin is strictly by specialist obstetric prescription.

interactions.effect: Massively elevated risk of major gastrointestinal and cerebral bleeding.
Increased risk of gastric ulceration; interferes with antiplatelet benefit.

administrationWarnings: Strictly prohibited in patients under 16 years of age with viral infections or fever.
Take after meals with a full glass of water.
Discontinue and seek urgent medical evaluation if tinnitus (ringing in ears) or black tarry stools develop.
dosageDisclaimer: Clinix does not calculate dosages. Always check the packaging leaflet and consult a registered pharmacist.

referenceSource.name: Ghana MoH Standard Treatment Guidelines / British Pharmacopoeia

approvedIndications: Treatment of susceptible anaerobic bacterial infections and protozoal infections (e.g. amoebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis)

contraindications.condition: Severe hypersensitivity to metronidazole or nitroimidazoles
contraindications.explanation: Risk of acute hypersensitivity reactions.
Causes a severe disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, throbbing headache, palpitations, vomiting, hypotension).

ageRestrictions.warning: Pediatric use requires specific weight-based clinician calculation.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Avoid during the first trimester of pregnancy unless considered essential by an obstetrician. Consult your doctor.

interactions.effect: Severe disulfiram-like reaction (acute tachycardia, violent vomiting, severe hypotension). Avoid alcohol during and for 48 hours after treatment.
Significantly potentiates anticoagulant effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk.

commonSideEffects: Unpleasant metallic taste in the mouth
administrationWarnings: PRESCRIPTION ONLY: Requires clinical diagnosis and prescription by a licensed practitioner.
Strictly avoid all alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.
Take with or after food with a full glass of water.
dosageDisclaimer: Requires prescription and weight/clinical indication determination by a clinician. Clinix does not calculate doses.

referenceSource.name: Ghana MoH Standard Treatment Guidelines / WHO Model List

approvedIndications: Symptomatic relief of allergic reactions, insect bites, acute urticaria, allergic rhinitis

contraindications.condition: Narrow-angle glaucoma or urinary retention (e.g. prostatic hypertrophy)
contraindications.explanation: Anticholinergic effects can precipitate acute glaucoma or acute urinary retention.
Potentiates anticholinergic and CNS depressant effects.

ageRestrictions.warning: Not recommended for children under 1 year of age without direct pediatrician supervision.

pregnancyPrecautions.warning: Use only if clearly needed and advised by a medical doctor. May cause neonatal irritability or tremors if taken in late pregnancy.

interactions.effect: Produces additive CNS depression, causing profound drowsiness and decreased reflexes.

administrationWarnings: Causes marked drowsiness: DO NOT drive, ride a bicycle, or operate machinery while taking this medicine.
Avoid alcoholic beverages entirely.
Keep strictly out of reach of children.
dosageDisclaimer: Consult product packaging leaflet or speak with your pharmacist for age-appropriate guidance.
